articles.title: US nutrition startup Berry Street merges with India's Healthify as GLP-1 trends upwards | TechCrunch
articles.text:
U.S. nutrition startup Berry Street said on Monday it has merged with Khosla Ventures-backed Indian startup Healthify to bank on the popular trend of people turning to GLP-1 drugs to lose weight.
The companies didn’t disclose the financial details of the deal. A report from JP Morgan published this year suggested that over 30 million people in the U.S. will be on GLP-1 by 2030.
The companies said Berry Street founder Noah Kotlove and Healthify founder Tushar Vashisht will act as co-CEOs of the new entity. In the U.S., the company will operate under the Berry Street banner, and in other markets like India, it will operate under the Healthify brand.
Healthify, which has raised over $150 million in funding, per Crunchbase, offers both AI-powered and human fitness and nutritional coaching via an app. Last year, the company expanded its operations in the U.S., and also started offering GLP-1-aided programs in India. The startup claims it has so far served more than 45 million customers.
“Healthify’s mission has been to put a dietitian in every human’s pocket. We have spent a decade proving that AI can drive life-changing outcomes at scale. Berry Street gives us the clinical backbone and the coverage infrastructure to deliver that promise to the U.S. market at a scale no one has achieved before,” Healthify’s CEO Vashisht said in a press release.
Berry Street has a network of over 2,000 clinics and offers insurance-covered GLP-1 care. The company last year raised $50 million in a fundraising round from Northzone, Sofina, and FJ Labs. This startup also provides AI-powered nutrition coaching and meal tracking, and claims it has served over 200,000 people in collaboration with Amazon, Walmart, and other platforms.
“By pairing AI with a nationwide network of expert clinicians, Healthify and Berry Street are building the platform that will redefine metabolic care, giving everyone access to daily nutrition guidance and expert dietitian advice,” Khosla Ventures’ founder Vinod Khosla said in a statement.

articles.title: Robotaxis are real now — so is the pushback
articles.text:
Robotaxis are expanding. So is the fight over the rules governing them.
Robotaxis are real now — so is the pushback
As more robotaxis hit the road, the fight over the rules governing the technology is intensifying.
Robotaxis are real now — so is the pushback
As more robotaxis hit the road, the fight over the rules governing the technology is intensifying.
In New York, Gov. Kathy Hochul withdrew a proposal earlier this year that would have opened the door to driverless robotaxis outside New York City after taxi drivers, unions, and state lawmakers opposed it. Six months later, commercial driverless service remains illegal in the state, and legalization efforts are stalled.
In DC, labor unions are fighting legislation that would legalize commercial robotaxis, while lawmakers are weighing a 200-vehicle cap and a 15-cent-per-mile fee that would fund Metro upgrades and aid workers displaced by autonomous vehicles. A July City Council hearing on the proposal stretched for a grueling 10 hours.
In San Francisco, Mayor Daniel Lurie, a vocal supporter of robotaxis, is now calling for tougher robotaxi regulations after Waymos repeatedly snarled traffic during emergencies and major events. And as of July, California police can now formally cite autonomous-vehicle manufacturers when their driverless cars break traffic laws.
And while Congress has yet to pass comprehensive robotaxi legislation, federal regulators have stepped up their scrutiny. The Trump administration’s National Highway Traffic Safety Administration recently warned autonomous-vehicle companies that vehicles unable to safely interact with police, firefighters, and other first responders pose a danger to the public.
Even in states that have broadly welcomed autonomous vehicles, governments are grappling with how to oversee them. Texas this year began enforcing new permitting requirements for commercial AV operators, while cities in Florida have complained that state preemption laws leave them with little power to respond to problems on their own streets.
Even in states that have broadly welcomed autonomous vehicles, governments are grappling with how to oversee them
Taxi drivers, labor unions, and safety advocates have fought autonomous vehicles for years. What’s changing is the scale and immediacy of the fight. Now that robotaxis have burst free from the pages of science fiction and onto actual city streets, policymakers are confronting a messier reality filled with questions about safety, regulation, growth, and jobs. They’re having to decide how quickly fleets should be allowed to expand, what companies must prove before they do, and how much control cities and states should have over their operations.
Waymo, the market leader, is currently operating more than 3,500 vehicles publicly in 11 US cities. Zoox — a purpose-built robotaxi without a steering wheel that bears a striking resemblance to a toaster — just began offering paid rides in Las Vegas and continues to offer free trips to users of its Explorer program in San Francisco as it collects feedback. It’s testing in a total of 10 cities and plans to extend the Explorer program to Austin and Miami later this year. Tesla, which began its Robotaxi rollout with a safety monitor aboard more than a year ago, appears to finally be growing its unsupervised fleet ahead of launching its purpose-built robotaxi, the Cybercab, later this month.
Still, for all the political attention, robotaxis remain a tiny share of the US ridehailing market. While Waymo now provides more than 500,000 paid rides a week, Uber handles about 40 million trips a day globally. At that scale, robotaxis haven’t yet displaced many driving jobs or fundamentally changed how cities move. But their visibility vastly exceeds their market share, especially when a driverless car stops in the wrong place during a blackout or interferes with an emergency response.
And the consequences could look very different as autonomous fleets grow from thousands of vehicles to hundreds of thousands. That’s why the battles taking shape across the country are increasingly about the terms of expansion: what companies have to prove before they grow, what they owe cities and workers, and how much control cities and states should have over their operations.
What the critics want
In many places, the robotaxi rollout has outpaced the rules governing it.
“Robotaxis are popping up all over the place,” said Shua Sanchez, national campaign director of SAVE-US, a nonprofit advocating for stricter state AV legislation in the absence of federal rules. “The state legislatures don’t have experience with this technology, and there aren’t good laws on the books to regulate them.”
SAVE-US is working with lawmakers in New Jersey and New York on a three-pronged approach. It wants multi-stage testing and commercial-deployment permits, under which companies would have to demonstrate their vehicles can operate safely with a small fleet before adding more cars, while continuing to share safety data after commercial service begins. It also wants autonomous vehicles to use multiple kinds of sensors, rather than relying on cameras alone (as Tesla does), and is calling for restrictions on marketing terms like “Autopilot” or “Full Self-Driving” for consumer driver-assist features when the systems still require human oversight.
The group isn’t opposed to autonomous vehicles, Sanchez said, but is “pro the safe development of technology.” He added that AV safety isn’t a settled question, and that even a strong record today doesn’t guarantee the same after a software or hardware change.
Sen. Ed Markey (D-MA), who has pushed for greater federal oversight of AVs, makes a similar argument about transparency.
“Autonomous vehicle companies are making huge claims about how their technology is going to save lives,” Markey told The Verge in a statement. “But right now, our regulatory structure amounts to this: we hope they’re telling the truth.”
Markey has investigated AV companies’ use of remote human operators and introduced legislation that would require them to regularly report safety data.
“Right now, our regulatory structure amounts to this: we hope they’re telling the truth.”
— Sen. Ed Markey
“Communities deserve transparency and consistent oversight before we let Big Tech invade their public roads,” he said.
But safety is only part of the fight. For labor groups, the stakes are also economic.
Peter Finn, Teamsters international vice president at large, called autonomous vehicles an “existential threat” to the work his members do. He pointed to the enormous number of jobs potentially affected by autonomous driving beyond rideshare drivers, including truckers, delivery drivers, and other commercial drivers.
Like other groups in the robotaxi debate, the Teamsters insist they aren’t opposed to new technology in principle. But that still leaves them staking out positions that would sharply constrain how autonomous vehicles are deployed.
That includes requiring heavy-duty autonomous vehicles like semitrucks to have a trained human operator aboard — legislation the Teamsters have twice pushed in California, only to see Gov. Gavin Newsom veto it. Finn said the Teamsters plan to pursue the issue again.
“If the technology is solely designed to automate and eliminate labor costs, the only entity benefiting from that is corporations,” Finn said.
The Teamsters’ immediate legislative priority isn’t robotaxis themselves so much as what it sees coming next.
To Finn, Waymo and Zoox are precursors to a much larger fight over autonomous driving. He pointed specifically to Zoox’s ownership by Amazon, arguing that similar technology could eventually be applied to package delivery.
Zoox and Waymo both said their current focus remains their robotaxi services.
Taken together, the objections go beyond any one safety rule or labor concern. AV resistance has become part of a broader backlash to Big Tech’s growing physical footprint, from data centers to Flock cameras. Companies are pouring enormous sums into new infrastructure, and many residents are still asking what, exactly, they get in return for having it in their communities.
Even robotaxi companies want rules
Robotaxi companies, meanwhile, are trying to get ahead of the backlash — and sidestep a patchwork of confusing state and local laws — by helping shape the rules themselves. That includes supporting certain regulations while pushing back on others they see as too restrictive.
“I want to unequivocally say we agree with the administrator and the administration and the regulatory agency. We need to be regulated,” Zoox CEO Aicha Evans recently said on Fox Business in response to NHTSA’s warnings about unsafe interactions with emergency vehicles.
Zoox said it is also trying to head off conflicts before entering new markets. Ron Thaniel, the company’s senior director of policy and regulatory affairs, said Zoox establishes lines of communication with local and state officials and conducts hands-on engagement with first responders before launching in a city. As the industry expands, he said, Zoox sees “an opportunity at the federal level to more uniformly regulate autonomous vehicles.”
Waymo told The Verge much the same thing.
“I think there definitely needs to be some regulation,” Waymo global head of public policy Justin Kintz said. “They’re powered by incredible technology that makes the world a safer place, but it still needs oversight from the federal government, from states, and from cities in the same way that they manage human drivers today.”
“I want to unequivocally say we agree with the administrator and the administration and the regulatory agency. We need to be regulated.”
— Zoox CEO Aicha Evans
Zoox and Waymo are hardly alone in wanting clearer rules. The Autonomous Vehicle Industry Association, which counts both companies as members, has said only about half of US states have passed laws that allow vehicles to operate without humans. The industry group believes states should establish a legal framework for AVs, require first-responder interaction plans, and set minimum requirements before vehicles can operate without a human driver. (The association didn’t respond to requests for more specifics.)
Waymo said it has long advocated for a national AV safety standard covering minimum testing requirements, vehicle design, and data sharing. Under its preferred system, the federal government would continue setting vehicle safety standards, while states would govern road rules and cities would handle local concerns like curb space, law enforcement, and emergency response.
The disagreements emerge in the details.
In Washington, DC, Waymo said it broadly supports Councilmember Charles Allen’s effort to establish a regulatory framework allowing commercial robotaxi service, including its goals of funding transit and helping workers transition as transportation becomes more automated. But it objects to parts of the current proposal.
Waymo said a 200-vehicle limit would probably be too small for a city the size of Washington. It could accept starting small, but wants regulators to let fleets grow as companies demonstrate safe performance rather than putting a permanent ceiling into law.
“I don’t think legislation needs to set a hard cap on that,” Kintz said, “or it’s going to lead to preventing important groups from being able to access the service when they need it.”
The company has been more receptive to the proposed 15-cent fee for every mile an autonomous vehicle travels. Kintz said Waymo supports “the fundamental principle of raising revenue” for transit and affected workers, though it raised concerns that a per-mile charge could become prohibitively expensive, particularly for smaller AV operators. An annual fee, it suggested, is one possible alternative.
Emergency response is another area where Waymo says it supports regulation, even as it argues that some of the work is already underway. After NHTSA called for stronger coordination between AV companies and first responders, Waymo said it immediately asked to participate in the agency’s discussions. The company said it already maintains dedicated first responder training programs and 24/7 priority lines for dispatchers and officers, while Kintz acknowledged that “we haven’t always got it right.”
“We haven’t always got it right.”
— Waymo global head of public policy Justin Kintz
Waymo is also trying to make the case that robotaxis can complement, rather than undermine, public transit. In a Streetsblog piece this month, Waymo policy development and research manager Arielle Fleisher argued the company has “common cause” with urbanists trying to reduce dependence on private cars. Waymo told The Verge that in San Francisco more than a third of its riders use the service to connect with public transportation. But research has also suggested that robotaxis could replace some trips that otherwise would have been taken on public transit, potentially undermining ridership rather than complementing it.
On labor, Waymo argues that automation will eliminate some tasks while creating others.
“These cars don’t clean, charge, fix themselves, code themselves,” Kintz said, pointing to jobs including fleet technicians, mechanics, remote support workers, and operations managers. Of course, simply taking the driver out of the driver’s seat could have huge economic implications. Earlier this month, Uber said that 10.2 million drivers and couriers earned money on its platform during the second quarter.
Kintz acknowledged that autonomous vehicles could eventually displace drivers and said Waymo was “eyes open” about that possibility. But he argued the change would happen over time and that unions could help build retraining and reskilling programs for affected workers.
Asked whether autonomous driving would ultimately create more jobs than it eliminated, Kintz said it was “too soon to tell.”
Notably Waymo has continued to expand as these fights play out. The California Public Utilities Commission this month cleared the company to expand driverless passenger service across parts of 18 counties, including Sacramento and San Diego and more of the Los Angeles and Bay Area regions.
For now, robotaxis are helping a very small number of Americans get around. The fights underway today are about what happens if they don’t stay that way.

articles.title: Taiwan reportedly indicted NVIDIA employees for exporting prohibited AI servers to China - Engadget
articles.text:
Taiwan reportedly indicted NVIDIA employees for exporting prohibited AI servers to China
The nine individuals are accused of 'severely damaged our nation's image,' prosecutors said.
Although the US has relaxed its restrictions on NVIDIA AI chip exports to China, illegal exports apparently still take place. Prosecutors in Taiwan just indicted nine individuals, including NVIDIA and Super Micro employees, for illegally bringing AI servers into China, Reuters reported.
The defendants "colluded with one another at various levels for enormous profit, illegally exporting high-end servers, increasing corporate compliance costs, and severely damaging our nation's international image," prosecutors from the northern city of Keelung said in a statement. They did this, the team added, despite being "fully aware" of NVIDIA and Super Micro's "rigorous" export control procedures.
Although NVIDIA is an American company, most of its chips are manufactured by the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), the world's largest chip maker by far. TSMC's latest Blackwell AI chips are manufactured in Phoenix, Arizona, but are still shipped to Taiwan for advanced packaging prior to final assembly.
The US has banned the sale of cutting-edge AI tech from NVIDIA and others to China since 2022. Recently, it has allowed sales to China of previous-generation products like H200 chips that are several years old. Taiwan is ultra-strict about exports of newer technology, lest it displease US regulators and, in particular, the Trump administration.
Despite Taiwan's clampdown, bad actors have found ways to get such chips into China. In one instance, $1 billion worth of server racks may have been shipped through Southeast Asian countries like Thailand or Malaysia to circumvent US export controls. In another case, the US charged three people with allegedly exporting $3.5 billion worth of AI servers to China, again by routing them through third-party countries.

articles.title: Teka - Chất lượng từ kỹ nghệ Đức và chính sách hậu mãi dài hạn
articles.text:
Với Teka, chất lượng không chỉ được tạo nên từ thiết kế và công nghệ, mà còn được đảm bảo xuyên suốt trong từng khâu lắp đặt và dịch vụ, để mỗi sản phẩm khi đến tay khách hàng đều đạt chuẩn về hiệu năng, độ hoàn thiện và sự an tâm khi sử dụng.
Ngày 18/8 vừa qua, Teka Việt Nam đã tổ chức chương trình đào tạo chuyên sâu về kỹ thuật cắt đá và lắp đặt bếp từ dành cho đội ngũ kỹ thuật viên cùng các đối tác trên toàn quốc, nhằm nâng cao năng lực thi công và chuẩn hóa chất lượng lắp đặt theo tiêu chuẩn Teka.
Đồng thời, thương hiệu cũng công bố chính sách hậu mãi đặc biệt dành riêng cho một số sản phẩm bếp từ, tiếp tục nâng cao chất lượng dịch vụ và củng cố sự an tâm cho khách hàng trong quá trình sử dụng.
An tâm nhờ sự chuẩn xác và thẩm mỹ
Với dòng bếp âm, mỗi đường cắt và thao tác lắp đặt đều góp phần quyết định đến cả hiệu năng vận hành lẫn vẻ đẹp của không gian bếp. Vì vậy, thương hiệu chú trọng chuẩn hóa quy trình thi công, để mỗi sản phẩm khi được lắp đặt không chỉ đúng kỹ thuật mà còn vừa vặn, hài hòa và giữ trọn tính thẩm mỹ cho căn bếp.
Tại chương trình, đội ngũ kỹ thuật viên được đào tạo chuyên sâu về sản phẩm và thực hành quy trình 8 bước lắp đặt theo tiêu chuẩn Teka: từ khâu chuẩn bị, đo đạc, tinh chỉnh mặt cắt cho đến các bước nghiệm thu và hướng dẫn bàn giao cho khách hàng.
Bên cạnh kỹ thuật chuyên môn, kỹ thuật viên được hướng dẫn sử dụng đúng thiết bị và trang phục bảo hộ cần thiết, góp phần đảm bảo an toàn trong suốt quá trình thi công.
Bảo chứng chất lượng từ hậu mãi dài hạn
Song song với việc nâng cao chất lượng thi công, Teka chính thức công bố 4 đặc quyền hậu mãi dành riêng cho dòng bếp từ Van Gogh Series và Elite Series (sắp ra mắt).
Tiếp nối tiêu chuẩn khắt khe từ sản phẩm, thương hiệu mở rộng sự chỉn chu đến dịch vụ hậu mãi, mang đến sự an tâm dài hạn cho khách hàng trong suốt quá trình sử dụng:
- Miễn phí cắt đá trên toàn quốc: hỗ trợ cắt đá miễn phí do đội ngũ kỹ thuật viên tay nghề cao đảm nhiệm, đảm bảo tính thẩm mỹ, công năng và độ an toàn cho không gian bếp.
- 3 năm bảo hành sản phẩm: Lời cam kết chắc chắn về chất lượng linh kiện và sự bền bỉ của một thương hiệu mang chuẩn mực Châu Âu, giúp người dùng an tâm tận hưởng trải nghiệm sử dụng lâu dài.
- 10 năm bảo hành mặt kính: Kế thừa nền tảng kỹ nghệ Đức, thương hiệu mang đến sự bảo chứng dài hạn cho chất lượng mặt kính, với khả năng chịu lực và chịu nhiệt được thiết kế để đồng hành cùng người dùng qua năm tháng.
- 365 ngày đổi mới: Khách hàng được hỗ trợ 1 đổi 1 trong vòng 365 ngày đối với các sự cố kỹ thuật liên quan đến vỉ mạch chính hoặc cuộn dây từ. Chương trình áp dụng từ ngày 1/9/2026 đến 1/9/2027.
Ra mắt bộ sưu tập Bếp từ Elite Series thế hệ mới
Trong tháng 9/2026, thương hiệu sẽ chính thức giới thiệu bộ sưu tập Bếp từ thế hệ mới - Elite Series.
Elite Series sở hữu 15 mức nhiệt cho khả năng điều chỉnh linh hoạt, Booster 2.500W giúp rút ngắn thời gian đun sôi, TrueEven Heating duy trì nhiệt ổn định ở mức thấp, lý tưởng cho các món hầm, kho cần thời gian nấu lâu, và InverterPlus tối ưu hiệu suất, tiết kiệm điện.
Dòng bếp được hoàn thiện với mặt kính EuroKera™ cao cấp từ Pháp và khung đế hợp kim chắc chắn, kết hợp giữa hiệu năng, độ bền và thẩm mỹ.
Không chỉ dừng lại ở khu vực chế biến, thương hiệu sẽ sớm trình làng Máy rửa chén thế hệ mới DSI-15T2-GB, sở hữu thiết kế nhỏ gọn với chiều cao chỉ 700 mm nhưng sức chứa lên đến 15 bộ, phù hợp với đa dạng thiết kế tủ bếp của người Việt.
Sản phẩm được trang bị công nghệ sấy khí nóng HeatDry Plus, hệ thống tia phun mạnh mẽ giúp làm sạch hiệu quả cùng khả năng vận hành êm ái với độ ồn thấp, sản phẩm mang đến khả năng làm sạch và sấy khô hiệu quả, trong khi vẫn duy trì không gian bếp yên tĩnh.
Qua đó, tiếp tục hoàn thiện hệ sinh thái thiết bị bếp, đáp ứng trọn vẹn các nhu cầu từ chuẩn bị, nấu nướng đến dọn dẹp.
Với nền tảng trăm năm kỹ nghệ Đức, tiêu chuẩn thi công được chuẩn hóa và dịch vụ hậu mãi dài hạn, Teka tiếp tục củng cố nền tảng tin cậy với khách hàng và đối tác, đồng thời từng bước nâng chuẩn trải nghiệm bếp tại Việt Nam.
(Nguồn: Teka Việt Nam)

articles.title: OpenAI loses a second sales leader in a week to Salesforce
articles.text:
OpenAI’s vice-president of sales in the Americas has resigned after five months in the job. Kaylin Voss is going back to Salesforce, according to The Information, which broke the story on Friday.
She left a week after her former boss. Denise Dresser, OpenAI’s chief revenue officer, walked out after nine months.
Both women came from Salesforce. Voss was Slack’s chief revenue officer before she joined.
She had been building a plan. Voss told Fortune a month ago that her team was segmenting customers into groups, among them telecommunications, retail, consumer goods and manufacturing. Cybersecurity was a focus, along with driving adoption and showing businesses a return.
Her old boss welcomed her back in public
“Welcome Home to The Ohana @KaylinVoss!” Marc Benioff posted on X, linking to the story about her departure. The post has been seen more than 135,000 times.
Amir Efrati of The Information followed with three words that did the same job. “Kaylin is going back to… Salesforce.”
The new man starts this week
OpenAI named Dali Rajic as chief revenue officer in mid-August, replacing Dresser. It is the company’s fifth C-suite change in a year, Emily Forlini reported for Fortune.
Rajic, 53, was president and chief operating officer at Wiz, the cybersecurity company Google bought this year for $32bn. He starts this week.
OpenAI investor Josh Kushner introduced him to the company, CNBC reported. Greg Brockman made the hire, according to a source Fortune spoke to. Brockman took over the revenue organisation in early July, after Fidji Simo stepped down from the number two job to focus on her health.
Why OpenAI wanted him
Rajic ran sales at AppDynamics from 2012, rising to chief revenue officer, and helped pitch that company to investors before Cisco bought it for $3.7bn the day before its planned market debut. He then spent five years at Zscaler as president of go-to-market, and moved to Wiz in 2024.
“If OpenAI is behind on enterprise, he is definitely the guy,” said Jyoti Bansal, the AppDynamics co-founder who first hired him.
A source with ties to Anthropic called the recruitment a coup, Fortune reported.
The cybersecurity connection
Rajic has spent a decade selling security software. That matters, because OpenAI wants to sell a lot more of it.
The company pitches businesses on using its models to prevent hacks and breaches, under a programme called Daybreak. It expanded Daybreak into multiple access tiers on 10 August.
How he sells
Rajic treats sales as a science rather than an art, former colleagues told Fortune. He declined to comment for that piece but confirmed the details in it. He follows MEDDPICC, a framework built at PTC in 1996 that scores a deal on metrics, the economic buyer, decision criteria, decision process, paper process, identified pain, champion and competition.
The method also predicts which salespeople will work out, within months of them starting, by counting first meetings booked and demos run.
“You don’t hesitate, you move them out of the business,” one former colleague said of those who miss the mark. The goal is a “very disciplined, highly predictable, scalable go-to-market machine”.
That predictability is what investors want to see before a listing.
Rajic learned it from John McMahon, whom one source called the godfather of enterprise sales, at BMC Software in the early 2010s. Index Ventures partner Shardul Shah has a name for the alumni network that came out of PTC.
“In the world of go-to-market, the equivalent is the PTC Mafia,” Shah told Fortune, comparing it to the PayPal one. It includes MongoDB’s chief executive and revenue chief, and Datadog’s.
The man himself
Rajic was born in Yugoslavia, in what is now Croatia, moved to Germany aged one and came to the United States at 16. He studied at Cal Poly Pomona and took an MBA at Northwestern.
Colleagues describe him as blunt, intellectual and relentless. “We would call him the Croatian Sensation,” one told Fortune, recalling a man who grabbed two hard-boiled eggs at Starbucks on the way to a meeting and called it breakfast.
He does not work a room at parties and does not chase speaking slots. He has no X account.
The job he is inheriting
Dresser oversaw a commercial organisation of roughly 1,200 people and ran it from the road, meeting clients herself, Fortune reported. She worked through weekends and pushed for granular reporting the company did not have.
Current and former staff describe constant change over the past few years and say keeping up is exhausting.
OpenAI acknowledges the number of leadership changes and says it is normal for a fast-growing company. Rajic was picked to lead the next phase of growth, and there is a strong bench of senior leaders, a spokesperson said. Dresser did not respond to Fortune’s requests for comment.
What the turnover is happening around
Enterprise now brings OpenAI more revenue than consumers, a milestone it reached ahead of plan, CNBC reported this month. The company is chasing market share held by Anthropic.
Anthropic’s revenue passed OpenAI’s for the first time last quarter. It is also preparing a listing that could match SpaceX’s record, and could file as soon as next month.
OpenAI’s own chief financial officer told staff the company will go public in 2027, or sooner. On the current timeline, its main rival gets there first.
The question nobody at OpenAI will answer
Rajic lives in Austin with his wife and three children, and expects to spend much of his time travelling and in San Francisco.
“It’ll be interesting to see if Dali is there in 12 or 18 months, or if he will burn out like so many other people do at OpenAI,” one source told Fortune. “That’s the open question.”
What has not been said
Neither Voss nor Dresser has given a public reason for leaving. OpenAI has not said who replaces Voss in the Americas, or whether the sales structure she was building survives her.
Salesforce has not said what role Voss returns to.

articles.title: I Watched a Family of Chickadees Grow Up in This Smart Birdhouse
articles.text:
Even though I've been a bird-watcher most of my life, nothing prepared me for the experience of witnessing—on my phone—the entire process of birds being born in my own backyard.
I’ve maintained a regular “dumb” nest box for years, the birthplace of generations of black-capped chickadees. I’ve seen them going in and out, but I always wondered what was happening in there, especially the year I opened up the box in the fall and found five deceased fledglings at the bottom. How could this have happened? I wondered.
Thanks to the Birdfy Nest Duo smart nesting box and its built-in thermometer and hygrometer, I now at least have an educated guess. (The poor things likely overheated during an early season heat wave.) Being able to watch the entire nesting operation from all angles, starting with excavation and egg-laying and ending in hatching and fledging, has been one of the most educational and entertaining bird-watching experiences I have ever had, and something I'd recommend to anyone interested in birds, nature, or just life science in general.
Eye Spy
Birdfy makes three smart nest boxes in addition to the Duo. The original, the Birdfy Nest, has one camera—located inside the box—and can only hang from an eye hook screwed into the top. There's also a version made out of solid fir in contrast to the others’ lightweight bamboo. I have also tested Birdfy’s artful Polygon, but persistent connection issues prevented me from using it this season.
I have not tested the first two single-camera versions, but I can't imagine not having a second camera outside the hole to see who's unexpectedly poking their head in. (At one point in my testing, it was a confused flicker; another, a curious starling—this is when I learned chickadees can hiss). It's also critical to be able to pole-mount the box to keep it away from predators.
The Nest Duo is substantial—16 inches tall and about 8 pounds—with one 1080p HD camera facing the nest entry hole on the exterior and another tucked discreetly inside the nest box itself. There's also an internal hygrometer (humidity) and thermometer (temperature) that show readings on the live view in Birdfy's easy-to-use app. There are four easy-to-install, screw-on entry hole sizes for different species, from 0.9 inches for wrens up to 2 inches for starlings or bluebirds, along with corresponding metal predator guards to prevent chewing. The entire side of the box opens with a latch for easy cleaning and access.
In the app, each screen capture appears as a split-screen image, which you can tap to view 20-second videos (with audio) of both the inside and the outside of the box. The videos are immediately downloadable and shareable—no subscription is needed.
The screen captures work much like one of Birdfy's smart bird feeders, but with images shunted to sections labeled “Prelude,” “Nesting,” “Brooding,” “Nestling,” “Fledgling,” and “End.” There seemed to be no rhyme or reason for what process the app thought was happening at the time (for example, if a nestling was simply turned around, the app asked if it should label it as “Fledgling”), but this story format was easy enough to ignore onscreen.
House Hunters
In March of this year, at the beginning of nesting season on the West Coast, I installed the Duo with the 1-inch entry hole on a pole stand and mounted the included solar panel below the box with hose clamps. Black-capped chickadees were consistently interested, popping in and looking around, but something was preventing them from staking a claim. It took me a while to realize they were looking askance at the holes on the metal tray “floor,” which is perforated for drainage. The idea is that this tray can be inserted into one of a series of slots to increase or decrease the nest cavity depth, depending on your local species' preference.

articles.title: The Witcher 4 developers target a 2028 release
articles.text:
CD Projekt Red is aiming to launch The Witcher 4 sometime in 2028, joint CEO Michał Nowakowski says in a new video. CD Projekt Red has been working on its next mainline Witcher title for years and has shown videos of it, but now the studio is providing a target release window for when the game might actually come out.
The Witcher 4 developers target a 2028 release
CD Projekt Red’s big Witcher sequel is still a couple years away.
There’s more new Witcher to come before The Witcher 4, though. At this week’s Gamescom event, CD Projekt Red will be showing off its upcoming Witcher 3 expansion, Songs of the Past, which is scheduled to release sometime in 2027. Songs of the Past is also set to be part of Gamescom’s Opening Night Live event hosted by Geoff Keighley, which kicks off at 2PM ET on Tuesday.
CD Projekt Red is also working on a multiplayer spinoff set in the universe of The Witcher that’s codenamed Project Siris. Earlier in August, the company confirmed that it laid off staff working on the game.

articles.title: Giá vàng nổi sóng bất chấp áp lực khổng lồ: Điều gì đang xảy ra?
articles.text:
Vàng tăng mạnh bất chấp dầu và lợi suất trái phiếu
Sau khi rơi về gần 4.330 USD/ounce vào giữa tuần trước, giá vàng giao ngay bất ngờ tăng dựng đứng trong ba phiên 19-21/8. Sáng nay, vàng tiếp tục leo thang.
Riêng phiên 19/8, vàng tăng từ khoảng 4.350 USD lên gần 4.500 USD/ounce, bất chấp giới đầu tư trước đó vẫn thận trọng với khả năng Cục Dự trữ Liên bang Mỹ (Fed) có thể tăng lãi suất thêm 1-2 lần trong phần còn lại của năm 2026.
Đến phiên cuối tuần 21/8, giá vàng giao ngay tiếp tục tăng mạnh và đóng cửa trên 4.600 USD/ounce, tương đương khoảng 145,7 triệu đồng/lượng, cao nhất khoảng 3 tháng rưỡi. Giá vàng giao tháng 12 thậm chí vượt 4.680 USD/ounce.
Trong nước, vàng SJC tăng khoảng 5 triệu đồng/lượng so với vùng đáy giữa tuần, lên 144,6 triệu đồng/lượng ở chiều mua và 147,6 triệu đồng/lượng ở chiều bán. Một số thương hiệu vàng nhẫn tăng khoảng 10 triệu đồng, lên 150,5-154,5 triệu đồng/lượng.
Điều đáng chú ý là đà tăng của vàng diễn ra trong bối cảnh những yếu tố thường gây bất lợi cho kim loại quý vẫn hiện diện.
Giá dầu tiếp tục đi lên do căng thẳng Mỹ-Iran. Phiên cuối tuần, WTI tăng gần 0,3% lên 87,1 USD/thùng, trong khi Brent tăng 0,65% lên 94,4 USD/thùng. Dầu tăng thường kéo theo lo ngại lạm phát Mỹ cao hơn, qua đó làm tăng khả năng Fed duy trì chính sách tiền tệ thắt chặt.
Lợi suất trái phiếu Mỹ cũng quay đầu tăng. Sau khi giảm từ đỉnh 5,333% xuống 5,18%/năm nhờ động thái can thiệp của Bộ Tài chính Mỹ, lợi suất trái phiếu 30 năm cuối tuần lại lên khoảng 5,275%.
Nhưng lần này, vàng dường như không còn phản ứng theo cách quen thuộc. Thay vì bị bán tháo khi lợi suất tăng, vàng vẫn vượt 4.600 USD/ounce.
Đằng sau diễn biến này có thể là một sự thay đổi trong mối quan tâm của thị trường: nhà đầu tư không chỉ lo lạm phát hay lãi suất, mà bắt đầu lo ngại về chính thị trường trái phiếu Mỹ và sức khỏe tài chính của nền kinh tế lớn nhất thế giới.
Khủng hoảng trái phiếu có thể mở đường cho chu kỳ tăng mới của vàng?
Một trong những tín hiệu đáng chú ý nhất tuần qua là động thái bất ngờ của Bộ Tài chính Mỹ.
Trong bối cảnh nợ công Mỹ lần đầu vượt 40.000 tỷ USD và lợi suất trái phiếu dài hạn tăng mạnh, Bộ Tài chính dưới sự điều hành của Bộ trưởng Scott Bessent tuyên bố tăng gấp đôi quy mô chương trình mua lại trái phiếu Chính phủ. Quy mô tối đa mỗi đợt được nâng từ khoảng 2 tỷ USD lên ít nhất 4 tỷ USD, tập trung vào các trái phiếu kỳ hạn 10-20 năm và 20-30 năm, vốn đang thiếu lực cầu.
Về bản chất, đây là cách Chính phủ Mỹ sử dụng nguồn vốn ngắn hạn để mua lại một phần trái phiếu dài hạn. Khi Chính phủ trở thành người mua lớn hơn, cầu đối với trái phiếu dài hạn được hỗ trợ, giá trái phiếu tăng và lợi suất có thể giảm.
Động thái này lập tức tạo hiệu ứng tích cực ban đầu: lợi suất giảm, chứng khoán phục hồi và USD suy yếu. Nhưng hiệu ứng không kéo dài. Đến cuối tuần, lợi suất 30 năm lại trở về quanh 5,27%, còn lợi suất 10 năm khoảng 4,7%.
Điều đó cho thấy vấn đề của thị trường trái phiếu Mỹ có thể mang tính cấu trúc hơn là một cú sốc ngắn hạn.
Cuộc đấu giá trái phiếu Kho bạc 30 năm trong tuần qua ghi nhận lợi suất trên 5,2%, mức cao nhất kể từ năm 2001. Một ngày trước đó, đợt phát hành trái phiếu 10 năm cũng có chi phí vay cao nhất kể từ năm 2007.
Lợi suất trái phiếu Mỹ kỳ hạn dài không chỉ là câu chuyện của Mỹ. Đây là một trong những mức giá tham chiếu quan trọng của chi phí vốn toàn cầu, gây sức ép lên người mua nhà, doanh nghiệp vay vốn và dòng tiền vào thị trường cổ phiếu. Ảnh hưởng là trên phạm vi toàn cầu.
Đáng chú ý hơn, thị trường đang xuất hiện khái niệm “Treasury Twist”. Bộ Tài chính Mỹ mua lại trái phiếu dài hạn trong khi tăng tỷ trọng sử dụng Treasury bills (tín phiếu kho bạc) và nợ ngắn hạn để đáp ứng nhu cầu tài trợ. Điều này có thể giúp giảm áp lực ở đầu dài của đường cong lợi suất, nhưng không giải quyết được thâm hụt ngân sách, không làm nợ liên bang biến mất và cũng không bảo đảm lạm phát dài hạn sẽ thấp.
Đây chính là điểm có thể tạo lợi thế cho vàng.
Nếu lợi suất trái phiếu Mỹ tiếp tục ở mức cao do nguồn cung nợ lớn, nhu cầu vốn ngày càng tăng và nhà đầu tư đòi hỏi mức bù rủi ro cao hơn, Fed sẽ phải cân nhắc kỹ hơn trước việc tiếp tục tăng lãi suất. Xác suất thị trường kỳ vọng Fed tăng lãi suất trong tháng 9 đã giảm từ trên 60% vài tuần trước xuống còn khoảng 39% vào ngày 23/8.
Trong khi đó, vàng đang được hưởng lợi từ nhiều yếu tố cùng lúc: nguy cơ lạm phát kéo dài, bất ổn địa chính trị, cuộc khủng hoảng nợ công và nguy cơ bất ổn trên thị trường trái phiếu.
Ray Dalio cũng cảnh báo nhà đầu tư nên giảm nắm giữ trái phiếu Mỹ và tăng tỷ trọng vàng, Bitcoin trong bối cảnh khủng hoảng nợ đang gia tăng.
Nếu một cuộc đua lợi suất trái phiếu thực sự hình thành trên phạm vi toàn cầu, nghịch lý có thể xảy ra: lợi suất trái phiếu tăng cao không còn là yếu tố kìm hãm vàng mà trở thành động lực thúc đẩy dòng tiền tìm đến vàng như một tài sản phòng thủ.
Sau khi tăng 65% trong năm 2025 và gần 30% chỉ trong tháng đầu năm 2026, vàng đã có một nhịp điều chỉnh rất mạnh từ đỉnh 5.600 USD/ounce xuống dưới 4.000 USD. Nhưng diễn biến mới nhất cho thấy chu kỳ tăng có thể chưa kết thúc.
Nếu áp lực nợ công tiếp tục gia tăng, thị trường trái phiếu Mỹ mất ổn định và Fed buộc phải thận trọng hơn với lãi suất, vàng có cơ sở duy trì xu hướng tăng. Khi đó, mốc 4.600 USD/ounce có thể không phải là đỉnh mới, mà chỉ là một bước trên hành trình tìm kiếm mặt bằng giá cao hơn.

articles.title: The biggest question about AI is what humans will do next
articles.text:
TL;DR
Technology advisor Monty McCoy argues that the most important question about AI is not whether machines will take jobs but what people will do with the time that opens up. He warns that removing the “whirlwind” of routine work without helping people develop new sources of meaning could create a vacuum filled by distraction, outrage, and division rather than creativity and connection.
When I had back surgery, I assumed recovery would be linear.
I thought each week would bring a little less pain, a little more mobility, and another step toward normal. Then I hit a setback. I had assumed I was further along than I actually was.
That experience has stayed with me because I think we are making a similar assumption about artificial intelligence.
We talk about the transition to an automated world as though it will follow a predictable path. AI capabilities will improve. Companies will adopt them. Autonomous systems will become more common. Workers will adjust. Eventually, much of the routine work that fills our days will be handled by machines.
I do not think it will happen that neatly.
The transition will be uneven. Some technologies will advance faster than expected. Others will stall. Industries will respond differently. Physical AI will introduce another layer of unpredictability as machines move beyond screens and into roads, factories, warehouses, homes, and public spaces.
There will be breakthroughs, disappointments, resistance, and surprises.
The question that interests me most, however, is what happens to us when the technology actually works.
For most people, work provides more than a paycheck. It gives the day a shape. It creates obligations, deadlines, and reasons to get up in the morning. Much of what occupies our working lives is what I call the whirlwind: the emails, meetings, administrative tasks, repetitive processes, and constant demands that consume our attention.
We complain about the whirlwind, yet we have also built our identities around it.
So what happens when it starts to disappear?
When the machines can handle the routine tasks, when software agents can manage processes that once required entire teams, when autonomous systems can perform physical work that once demanded human labor, what fills the space left behind?
That is a deeply personal question before it becomes an economic or political one.
When the whirlwind stops, who do you become?
I do not think most people will automatically use that freedom to discover some grand new purpose. We like to imagine that if technology gave us more time, we would spend it learning, creating, traveling, volunteering, or deepening our relationships.
Maybe some of us would.
Many others might simply fill the space with more noise.
We already live in an economy built around capturing attention. Our phones can fill any empty moment. Social platforms can provide an endless stream of content. Entertainment is available whenever we want it. If automation removes more of the structures that currently organize our days, there is no guarantee that people will use the resulting freedom well.
That possibility concerns me more than the idea of robots taking jobs.
A society with more free time could become more creative, more connected and more human. It could also become more distracted, fragmented and restless. The technology itself will not determine which direction we take.
Our choices will.
This is why I have become increasingly interested in the idea of ownership.
As AI becomes embedded in everyday life, people will have to think more deliberately about what they control. That includes their data, certainly, but it also includes their time, attention, skills, and sense of purpose.
We have become accustomed to handing pieces of our lives to systems because doing so is convenient. We accept the terms, click the button, and move on. The scale of that exchange is about to change dramatically.
The more capable our systems become, the more important individual agency becomes.
I am genuinely excited about that future.
I can imagine an older person retaining independence because autonomous transportation gives them mobility long after driving becomes difficult. I can imagine technology removing some of the physical limitations that have historically determined what people can do as they age. I can imagine people spending less of their lives on repetitive tasks and more of them pursuing work and experiences that require judgment, curiosity, creativity, and human connection.
That is an extraordinary opportunity.
But opportunity does not automatically become fulfillment.
If we remove the structures that have occupied people’s time without helping them develop new sources of meaning, we could create a vacuum. And vacuums tend to get filled.
They can be filled by entertainment. By outrage. By endless consumption. By tribalism. By political and social division. They can also become a source of anxiety between people who benefit from automation and people who believe they have been pushed aside by it.
I am not predicting that outcome. I am arguing that we should take it seriously while we still have time to shape what comes next.
The mistake would be to assume that technological progress and human progress are the same thing.
They are related, but they are not automatic.
The coming transition will require us to think about questions that technology cannot answer for us. What is a good life when efficiency is no longer the primary constraint? What gives a person meaning when employment occupies less of their identity? What happens to communities when fewer people share the same daily routines? How do we make sure greater technological capability produces greater human agency?
I do not have a simple answer to those questions.
I think that is precisely why we need to start asking them.
My recovery taught me that progress rarely follows the schedule we imagine for it. The body has its own timeline. So will this technological transition.
There will be moments when AI advances faster than society expects, followed by moments when adoption slows, or unexpected consequences force us to reconsider the path.
We should embrace the possibilities without assuming the outcome is predetermined.
The future will not simply happen to us. We will have a role in deciding what fills the space when the whirlwind stops.
And we should start claiming the controls before the systems do.

articles.title: ESPN streaming plans are getting more expensive
articles.text:
ESPN is hiking the price of its subscription on September 17th, a change that will also impact its bundles with Disney Plus. In a support page spotted earlier by Sports Media Watch, ESPN says its ad-supported Select membership will cost $13.99 instead of $12.99 / month, while its Unlimited plan will rise to $31.99 from $29.99 / month.
ESPN streaming plans are getting more expensive
Starting September 17th, a subscription to ESPN Unlimited will cost $31.99 per month.
The annual ESPN Select plan is also going to $139.99 from $129.99 / year, and the annual Unlimited tier is increasing to $319.99 from $299.99 / year. Meanwhile, Disney Plus bundles with ESPN Select are going up in price as well. Here’s a rundown of the changes:
- Disney Plus (with ads), Hulu (with ads), and ESPN Select: $21.99 / month, up from $19.99 / month.
- Disney Plus (ad-free), Hulu (ad-free), ESPN Select: $32.99 / month, up from $29.99.
- Legacy Disney Plus (ad-free), Hulu (ad-free), and ESPN Select: $27.99 / month, up from $24.99 / month.
Disney Plus bundles with ESPN Unlimited aren’t affected. Last week, Axios reported that about 80 percent of Unlimited subscribers signed up through the bundle with Disney Plus and Hulu.
Though Disney last raised prices across its bundles last year, this is the first increase for ESPN, which rolled out its standalone streaming subscription last August. As part of the launch, ESPN updated its mobile app with a TikTok-like feed of videos and a personalized version of SportsCenter. ESPN also launched multiview in its app on major smart TV platforms.

articles.title: These Home Theater Projectors Give the Cinema Some Tough Competition
articles.text:
I've seen some of the best movies and tested some of the best home projectors this year. Massively entertaining films like The Odyssey, Project Hail Mary, and Toy Story 5 have made 2026 a standout year for movies, and new home theater projectors like the Xgimi Titan Noir Max and the AWOL Vision Aetherion Max have upped the game in terms of beautiful, cinematic, color-accurate images at home.
I've been reviewing the best TVs and projectors for years. That's why I put these latest home theater projectors to the test, running benchmarks to check for vividness, brightness, skin tone variations, and whether dark scenes look too washed out. I watched countless Netflix movies and 4K Blu-ray films—all for the cause. My main takeaway? These top models are giving the local cinema something to worry about. Bring some popcorn and a comfortable recliner, and you're basically there.
For more TV recommendations based on our expert testing, check out our related guides, including the Best RGB TVs, Best TVs, Best Large TVs, Best OLED TVs, and Best Cheap TVs. If you’re really undecided, read our guide on How to Buy the Right TV in 2026.
Love WIRED? Add us as a preferred source on Google to see more of us.
Best Overall
Picking the best projector was not easy, especially since there's so much competition. The Xgimi Titan Noir Max won me over because of the dynamic, self-adjusting iris. As you watch a movie or show, the projector adjusts to allow more light in (for bright scenes) or closes to reduce light (for dark scenes). For example, during a nighttime sequence in the movie Hoppers on Disney+, the iris will close to make the blacks and grays look dark and richly detailed. That feature alone sets the Titan Noir Max apart.
But it’s also highly capable in many other ways. It has an outstanding 10,000:1 native contrast ratio and a 7,000-lumen brightness rating, which helped it blast through all of my benchmarks and test scenarios. An early morning scene in the movie The Creator looked exactly like I would expect it to in real life, showing texture on the seaside cliffs. Even in a sun-drenched room, battle scenes in the movie War Machine looked bright and clear—outperforming the Hisense XR10 model.
More functionally, it has four adjustable feet that allow you to adjust the height or even set the projector on a side table and angle it toward a wall.
One downside is that, like many projectors, it doesn't natively run a streaming OS like Google TV, but I prefer to connect a Blu-ray player or Google TV Streamer anyway.
| Specs |  | 
|---|---|
| Refresh rate | 240 Hz | 
| Weight | 18 pounds | 
| HDMI ports | 3 | 
| Light source | Triple laser | 
Best for Gaming
I’ll never forget the first time I played the game 007 First Light projected on a wall in my house using the Hisense XR10. An ocean scene looked bright blue and realistic, thanks to the excellent color processing on this projector. I felt very little lag using the low-latency mode, and the built-in speakers (the best I've tested on a projector) never felt lacking.
The big and boxy XR10 is exactly what I would expect a high-end cinema projector to look like. It’s heavy at 23.4 pounds, but that’s because of its massive speaker and lens. Although I prefer the long adjustable legs on the Xgimi Titan Noir Max, the XR10 is stable and has a nicely subdued dark metallic look.
The iris is adjustable (in seven different ways) to allow more light in or to make darker scenes even more vivid. Games in particular looked rich and colorful, including one of my all-time favorites, Senua's Saga: Hellblade II. A beach scene had a texture and moodiness that was truly jaw-dropping.
I loved watching the movie Awake on Netflix, which is dark in almost every scene. (It was the first time I noticed a guy in the background of one scene wearing a blue shirt.) Most projectors render these dark scenes without enough contrast, but the XR10 makes them look stunning.
The XR10 is a monster of a home cinema projector, with only the Titan Noir Max performing just a bit better on color and brightness. And you do need to adjust the iris manually in the settings, though (unlike the automatic adjustments of the Titan Noir Max).
| Specs |  | 
|---|---|
| Refresh rate | 240 Hz | 
| Weight | 23 pounds | 
| HDMI ports | 3 | 
| Light source | Triple laser | 
Best for Movies
Leica has a rich history making cameras, and this Leica Cine Play 1 projector is a showcase of that superior craftsmanship. The Leica Summicron lens renders ultra-realistic video with extreme clarity and exceptional color accuracy. I watched Hoppers in a windowless testing room, and the furry creatures all looked stunningly realistic—you could even see individual strands of fur cleanly.
That’s why I think it's the best projector for movies and shows. Colors pop on the screen like you are watching in a theater. This model exceeds the BT.2020 color gamut spec by 107 percent, and you can tell in movies like Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse. In one segment, the reds and blues looked even more vivid than I remembered at the theater.
The compact size (about the same as a large lunch box) and good portability (weighing about 15 pounds) were two highlights for me. I also like the metallic design with the iconic red Leica logo on top. The projector can easily sit on a table, or you can add the Cine Play 1 Floor Stand for $495. The power cord connects to the base of the stand, which makes for a very clean setup.
It's impressive, but not as impressive in a bright room, unfortunately—this projector is best utilized at night. And it lacks the dynamic iris of the Titan Noir Max (which is, admittedly, much pricier).
| Specs |  | 
|---|---|
| Refresh rate | 120 Hz | 
| Weight | 15 pounds | 
| HDMI ports | 2 | 
| Light source | Triple laser | 
Best Budget
I had to double check the price of the BenQ W4100i because it's so much cheaper than my other top picks. Yet, of all the home cinema projectors I've tested in the last few months, the quick and easy setup on this model, plus a few unusual perks, made it a top pick.
It's easy to configure, even though it uses the older Android TV operating system. I asked the onboard Google Assistant bot to start the install process and it only took a few minutes to do the whole thing. While the dark gray enclosure is understated, I liked how easy it was to adjust the focus and throw distance using analog levers on the top of the projector.
At this price, the W4100i is not meant to compete with the titans of home cinema like the Hisense XR10, and it matches an older color gamut spec (Rec.709). The lumens rating is only 3,200, far below the Titan Noir Max's 7,000.
Still, there are a few interesting perks with the BenQ W4100i. It has a mode that can match the 24p frame rate of movies for a more fluid look. With the refresh rate cranked to 240 Hz, playing the game NTE on my gaming laptop, I came to realize just how much I like using this projector for low-latency gaming. My controller flicks were rendered immediately during chaotic battle scenes.
I’m not sure why BenQ insists on still using a dongle attachment for the operating system. You can skip it altogether if you use one of the HDMI ports for a Blu-ray player or another device. In the end, the lower-than-expected price, low latency, and easy setup are what sold me on this BenQ.
| Specs |  | 
|---|---|
| Refresh rate | 240 Hz | 
| Weight | 22 pounds | 
| HDMI ports | 2 | 
| Light source | LED | 
Honorable Mentions
Epson Lifestudio Grand Plus for $3,800: A powerhouse for movies and shows, this short-throw projector can be set right next to your projector screen or blank wall and display a huge image. It also, surprisingly, has Google Gemini built in, which can do some surprising tasks like create slideshows, fit with animations, original images, voice-overs, and more.
AWOL Aetherion Max RGB Laser UST Projector for $4,449: I’m currently in the middle of testing this short-throw model, and it is an engineering marvel. The incredible 6000:1 contrast ratio and triple-laser light source are just the beginning. I’ve been impressed by the color accuracy, brightness, deep blacks, and extreme clarity across the entire image.
Frequently Asked Questions
Why Use a Home Theater Projector?
It’s an eternal debate—should you pull the shades, fire up a home theater projector, and watch a movie like you’re at the local cineplex? Or is it better to use a massive OLED or RGB television that will show a clearer image during a sunny day? Here’s my take after testing tons of the latest projectors and TVs: I prefer projectors for movies because I can max out the screen size to 120 inches or more. There’s just nothing like watching a 12-foot projected image of a movie with Dolby Atmos surround sound at home.
What Do You Need to Use a Home Theater Projector?
The short answer is quite simple: You just need a white wall. Purists will say a true home cinema experience requires a projector screen and a windowless room, and I have a testing room just for that purpose. However, all of the models I’m recommending are so bright and colorful that they perform quite well on a large wall without needing a projector screen. I do recommend room-darkening shades, though, because a darker room does create a better image.
Why Are Home Theater Projectors So Expensive?
Consumer-grade home theater projectors cost around $3,000 or more. In my experience, the latest large OLED and RGB televisions can easily cost just as much. I strongly recommend sticking to the $3,000 price point for a home cinema projector, though, because many midrange models (e.g., under $2,000) don’t look that colorful or bright. They also suffer from some serious contrast problems. For serious movie and TV fans, I’d avoid projectors that cost less than $1,000.

articles.title: Giá xăng dầu hôm nay 24/8: Thế giới quay đầu giảm, trong nước tăng
articles.text:
Giá dầu thế giới hôm nay
Mở cửa phiên giao dịch đầu tuần này (24/8), giá dầu thế giới đảo chiều đi xuống, sau khi tăng mạnh vào tuần trước.
Dữ liệu từ Oilprice cho hay, vào lúc 6h51' ngày 24/8 (giờ Việt Nam), giá dầu Brent được niêm yết ở mức 93,51 USD/thùng, giảm 0,93% so với phiên liền trước. Còn giá dầu WTI được giao dịch ở mức 86,21 USD/thùng, hạ 0,98% so với phiên liền trước.
Trong tuần trước, giá dầu thế giới tăng mạnh, với cả 5 phiên đều đi lên. Tính chung trong tuần qua, giá dầu Brent tăng 6,39%, còn giá dầu WTI tăng 5,66%.
Giá dầu Brent đóng cửa tuần qua ở mức 94,39 USD/thùng, trong khi giá dầu WTI kết tuần trước ở mức 87,06 USD/thùng.
Tuy giảm nhẹ ở đầu phiên hôm nay nhưng dầu mỏ vẫn đang được giao dịch ở vùng giá cao trong bối cảnh lo ngại gián đoạn nguồn cung tại Trung Đông tiếp tục bao trùm thị trường, trong khi hoạt động vận chuyển qua eo biển Hormuz vẫn chưa trở lại bình thường.
Giới đầu tư đang theo dõi chặt chẽ những biến động về lượng dầu thô dự trữ, yếu tố được coi là vùng đệm ứng phó với các cú sốc về nguồn cung.
Theo công ty nghiên cứu dữ liệu Kpler, tổng tồn kho dầu thô toàn cầu, bao gồm cả dự trữ chiến lược và kho thương mại, đạt khoảng 3,45 tỷ thùng tính đến ngày 21/8, giảm 6% so với cuối tháng 2, thời điểm xung đột Trung Đông bùng phát.
Trong đó, tồn kho dầu tại Nhật Bản giảm 18%, tại Mỹ giảm 15%, tại Trung Quốc giảm khoảng 5%.
Trong khi đó, khả năng Mỹ trở thành nguồn cung thay thế vẫn chưa chắc chắn.
Cơ quan Thông tin Năng lượng Mỹ (EIA) cho hay, xuất khẩu dầu thô của Mỹ trong tuần kết thúc vào ngày 7/8 chỉ đạt 3,05 triệu thùng/ngày, thấp nhất trong 9 tháng.
Giá xăng dầu trong nước hôm nay
Giá bán các mặt hàng xăng dầu phổ biến tại thị trường trong nước vào hôm nay (24/8) được áp dụng như sau:
Theo kỳ điều hành ngày 20/8, giá xăng E5 RON92 tăng 598 đồng/lít, giá bán lẻ không cao hơn 21.833 đồng/lít.
Trong khi giá xăng E10 RON95-III tăng 549 đồng/lít, giá bán không cao hơn 22.668 đồng/lít.
Tương tự, giá dầu diesel 0.05S tăng 1.310 đồng/lít, giá bán lẻ không cao hơn 28.543 đồng/lít.
Còn giá dầu mazut 180CST 3.5S tăng 933 đồng/kg, giá bán không cao hơn 17.689 đồng/kg.
Theo dữ liệu từ Bộ Công Thương, giá bán lẻ xăng dầu tại Việt Nam hiện ở mức thấp hơn so với một số nước có chung đường biên giới.
Liên bộ Công Thương - Tài chính đang tiếp tục theo dõi sát diễn biến thị trường để thông báo giá xăng dầu phù hợp, đúng chỉ đạo và kịp thời đề xuất Chính phủ, Thủ tướng Chính phủ về các giải pháp bình ổn giá xăng dầu.

articles.title: Australian data centres are closing in on 13% of the grid
articles.text:
Australian data centres will take 13% of the country’s main electricity market by 2035-36, up from 3% today. That is almost a sevenfold rise in a decade, according to the Australian Energy Market Operator. Keira Wright reported the forecast for Bloomberg.
The figure lands in AEMO’s annual Electricity Statement of Opportunities. The document is the operator’s read on whether supply will meet demand across the National Electricity Market over the coming decade, and it is the one utilities and governments plan against.
The number
Data centres will draw 34 terawatt hours a year from the National Electricity Market by 2035-36, on AEMO’s projection. The market operator published the forecast at a moment when the country is closing most of its old baseload.
Roughly 13 gigawatts of coal-fired plant will retire within the decade. Almost 2 gigawatts of gas generation will go with it.
Those two sets of numbers do not subtract from each other. The data centre forecast counts energy over a year, in terawatt hours. The retirements count capacity at a moment, in gigawatts. They describe different things.
Why data centres bother a grid operator
“Data centers are particularly influential because they operate relatively consistently throughout the day and across seasons, similar to large industrial loads,” AEMO said in its report.
That flatness is the problem. A steady draw presses on the system during the hours when everyone else has switched off. Those are the hours when the grid runs thinnest.
Most large loads follow a pattern a planner can anticipate. Factories run shifts, households cook dinner, air conditioning tracks the weather. A rack of accelerators does none of that.
What is being built
The outlook is not all strain. Generation and storage connections more than doubled last year’s record, and AEMO says that has improved the reliability picture.
Last year was already a high-water mark. Record clean energy additions eased blackout fears in August 2025, Bloomberg reported at the time. This year beat it.
About 9 gigawatts of new generation and storage reached full output in 2025-26. That is double the year before.
“A significant amount of new capacity is expected to be delivered between now and the early 2030s,” AEMO chief executive Daniel Westerman said in a statement. It will help “replace retiring generation and support growing electricity demand”, he said.
“Beyond 2030, the next wave of investment will be critical to maintaining reliability.”
A third of the pipeline vanished
Developers have since cancelled more than a third of the data centre projects AEMO listed last year, according to the report.
That is a useful correction to every capacity forecast in this sector, including this one. Announced projects and built projects are different populations.
It also cuts both ways. A pipeline that shrinks by a third in a year could shrink again, or it could refill faster than the wires arrive.
The money behind it
Commonwealth Bank of Australia estimates the country’s data centre buildout could reach A$150bn, about $108bn, by 2030.
Australia wants that investment. It is trying to capture the economic benefits of the buildout while limiting the strain on its grid and its water supplies, Bloomberg reported. That tension runs through the whole file.
Demand arrives faster than wires
A data centre can switch on long before the infrastructure to power it exists. The United States Studies Centre has put numbers on that mismatch for Australia.
The Clean Energy Finance Corporation has flagged what follows. Its report names bottlenecks, higher prices for consumers, and more reliance on fossil fuels than anyone planned for.
The politics is unresolved
The federal government is pushing to make new data centres run on renewable energy. Bloomberg reported that doubling down earlier this month. Some regional administrations object.
Anthony Albanese will use Wednesday’s national cabinet to reassure premiers about a new AI law, according to the Guardian. He will promise that federal approval rules complement state ones rather than override them.
The conservative governments of Queensland and the Northern Territory have been the loudest objectors. A climate expert told the paper Australia has “one shot to get the rules right”.
The argument is not new. Australia’s world-first data centre rules needed every state to agree, and two said no in July.
Some builders are going around the grid
Not every project waits for a connection. A gas-rich outback station could host a $28bn off-grid AI data centre. It would generate its own power rather than queue for someone else’s.
That solves the operator’s problem by removing the site from the operator’s system. It does not solve the emissions one.
Everyone else has the same fight
The pattern repeats wherever the buildout lands. An operator or a government looks at the connection queue, finds it larger than the wires, and reaches for a pause or an audit.
Texas called itself the epicentre of AI, then froze new connections pending an audit.
Scotland weighed a moratorium that would have frozen new datacentres and threatened the UK’s AI plan.
In Europe the constraint is queueing rather than politics, and it has pushed 63% of new capacity out of the five established markets.
What the forecast does not settle
AEMO has published a demand projection, not a build schedule. The 34 terawatt hours assumes a pipeline that has already lost a third of its projects once.
The report does not say which sites make it, who supplies their power, or what happens to the 13% share if the next wave of investment Westerman describes does not arrive.
Nor does it settle the question the premiers are arguing about on Wednesday, which is who gets to say yes to a data centre in the first place.

articles.title: Raspberry Pi shares its official tutorial for making a cyberdeck
articles.text:
Raspberry Pi’s head of social, Ashley Whittaker, acknowledged the cyberdeck trend today, saying “we haven’t been able to get away from cyberdecks this year.” Tiny portable computers made out of things like purses, jewelry boxes, and other thrifted or recycled parts have gone viral on TikTok and other social media platforms over the past year, and Raspberry Pi now has its own guide to building one of the homemade computers.
Raspberry Pi shares its official tutorial for making a cyberdeck
Homemade mini computers have been going viral lately, and this guide could give the trend a boost.
Raspberry Pi has also increased its prices multiple times this year due to rising costs for RAM and other components, which could be another reason to support this growing market of active and would-be hobbyists. The 16GB version of the Raspberry Pi 5 included in the company’s official cyberdeck guide got a $100 price hike in April, nearly as much as the board’s original $120 price.
Raspberry Pi’s cyberdeck guide includes a parts list and detailed assembly instructions, but sticks to a fairly simple design using a plain black Pelican-style case. As content creators are proving, though, you can make a cyberdeck out of just about anything. Annike Tan, whose cyberdecks have attracted millions of views on TikTok, continues to upgrade her “mermaid” purse cyberdeck with new design details and even added a USB hub.

articles.title: Giá vàng trong nước đi sau, tăng chậm hơn thế giới: Người dân lạnh nhạt với vàng?
articles.text:
Giá vàng thế giới ngày 22/8 tiếp tục tăng mạnh, vượt mốc 4.600 USD/ounce.
Trong nước, giá vàng cũng tăng theo, nhưng mức tăng chậm hơn. Mở cửa phiên sáng, vàng miếng và vàng nhẫn thương hiệu SJC đồng loạt tăng 600.000 đồng/lượng so với phiên trước, lần lượt lên 144,6-147,6 triệu đồng/lượng và 144,1-147,1 triệu đồng/lượng (mua vào - bán ra).
Sau đó, giá vàng nhẫn được một số thương hiệu tiếp tục điều chỉnh tăng, tiến sát mốc 150 triệu đồng/lượng (bán ra).
Giá vàng thế giới quy đổi lên khoảng 146 triệu đồng/lượng, thấp hơn giá bán vàng miếng SJC khoảng 1,6 triệu đồng/lượng. Diễn biến này cho thấy mức tăng của giá vàng trong nước đang thấp hơn giá thế giới, khiến chênh lệch giữa hai thị trường tiếp tục thu hẹp.
Vì sao vàng trong nước tăng chậm hơn thế giới?
Trao đổi với PV VietNamNet, chuyên gia kinh tế Nguyễn Quang Huy, CEO Khoa Tài chính - Ngân hàng, Trường Đại học Nguyễn Trãi (NTU) cho rằng, việc giá vàng thế giới vượt 4.600 USD/ounce nhưng giá trong nước tăng chậm hơn là diễn biến đáng chú ý, song không bất thường.
Theo ông Huy, giá vàng thế giới phản ánh rất nhanh dòng tiền quốc tế, diễn biến của đồng USD, lợi suất trái phiếu và kỳ vọng về lãi suất. Trong khi đó, giá vàng trong nước còn chịu tác động của cung - cầu thực tế, tỷ giá, thanh khoản, tồn kho và tâm lý người mua. Vì vậy, giá trong nước không nhất thiết phải tăng cùng tốc độ với giá thế giới.
Điểm quan trọng, theo ông, là sức mua trong nước hiện nay chưa tăng tương ứng với đà tăng của giá quốc tế. Khi vàng lên mặt bằng rất cao, người dân có xu hướng thận trọng hơn và hạn chế mua đuổi. Doanh nghiệp kinh doanh vàng phải cân đối giữa giá đầu vào, lượng tồn kho và khả năng tiêu thụ. Nếu nâng giá quá nhanh trong khi sức mua chưa theo kịp, thanh khoản có thể giảm.
Bên cạnh đó, khi chênh lệch giữa giá vàng trong nước và thế giới đã thu hẹp đáng kể, dư địa để giá vàng trong nước tăng thêm phần chênh lệch cũng không còn nhiều. Vì vậy, mỗi nhịp tăng của giá thế giới chưa chắc được chuyển hóa ngay thành mức tăng tương ứng trong nước.
“Tôi cho rằng đây là tín hiệu tương đối tích cực: giá vàng trong nước đang phản ánh rõ hơn cung - cầu thực tế, thay vì chỉ chạy theo tâm lý quốc tế”, ông Huy đánh giá.
TS Lê Bá Chí Nhân, chuyên gia kinh tế, cũng cho rằng diễn biến hiện nay cho thấy giá vàng trong nước ngày càng vận động sát hơn với giá vàng quốc tế, thay vì duy trì mức chênh lệch quá lớn như trước.
Theo ông, có 3 nguyên nhân chính. Thứ nhất, chênh lệch giá vàng trong nước đang được thu hẹp. Khi nguồn cung và cơ chế quản lý thị trường được cải thiện, doanh nghiệp không còn nhiều dư địa để cộng mức chênh lệch lớn vào giá vàng. Vì vậy, giá trong nước có thể tăng nhưng không nhất thiết cùng tỷ lệ với giá thế giới.
Thứ hai, cung - cầu nội địa ngày càng đóng vai trò quan trọng. Trong khi giá vàng thế giới chịu tác động bởi nhu cầu trú ẩn, bất ổn địa chính trị, kỳ vọng chính sách tiền tệ và diễn biến USD, thị trường Việt Nam còn phụ thuộc vào sức mua, lượng vàng lưu thông, khả năng cung ứng và tâm lý nhà đầu tư. Do đó, độ trễ giữa hai thị trường là bình thường.
Thứ ba, doanh nghiệp vàng thận trọng hơn khi định giá. Trước biến động nhanh của giá thế giới, doanh nghiệp phải tính đến rủi ro giá đảo chiều và tồn kho, nên thường điều chỉnh giá có kiểm soát và duy trì biên độ mua - bán để phòng ngừa biến động.
Ông Nhân nhìn nhận, chênh lệch giữa giá vàng trong nước và thế giới thu hẹp xuống còn vài triệu đồng mỗi lượng là tín hiệu tích cực, cho thấy quá trình liên thông giữa hai thị trường đang tốt hơn, giảm phần “giá độc quyền” hoặc “phần bù khan hiếm” trước đây.
Giá vàng sắp tới ra sao?
Trước câu hỏi liệu doanh nghiệp vàng có cố tình không đẩy giá lên quá nhanh vì lo người dân chốt lời, bán vàng và chuyển tiền sang gửi tiết kiệm khi lãi suất huy động tăng, ông Lê Bá Chí Nhân cho rằng đây có thể là một yếu tố nhưng không phải nguyên nhân chính.
Theo ông, cần nhìn vấn đề từ cung - cầu và cơ chế hình thành giá của thị trường vàng.
Ông lý giải, doanh nghiệp kinh doanh vàng không nhất thiết điều chỉnh giá tăng tương ứng ngay với giá thế giới. Họ phải quản trị đồng thời rủi ro giá, rủi ro tồn kho và rủi ro thanh khoản. Nếu mua vàng vào ở mức cao rồi thị trường thế giới bất ngờ đảo chiều, lượng vàng tồn kho có thể tạo ra rủi ro lớn.
Vì vậy, trong những phiên biến động mạnh, doanh nghiệp thường điều chỉnh giá bán thận trọng hơn và kiểm soát chênh lệch mua - bán.
Bên cạnh đó, khi giá vàng tăng mạnh trong thời gian dài, một bộ phận nhà đầu tư có thể chuyển từ mua tích lũy sang chốt lời. Lượng vàng bán ra tăng sẽ cải thiện nguồn cung, qua đó khiến giá trong nước tăng chậm hơn giá thế giới.
Mặt bằng lãi suất tiền gửi tương đối hấp dẫn cũng tạo thêm kênh cạnh tranh dòng tiền với vàng, nhất là với nhóm nhà đầu tư ưu tiên bảo toàn vốn và dòng tiền ổn định.
“Tuy nhiên, không nên hiểu rằng doanh nghiệp đang cố tình ‘ghìm’ giá vàng. Giá trong nước vẫn phải phản ánh giá thế giới, tỷ giá, cung - cầu và chi phí kinh doanh. Việc giá thế giới tăng mạnh trong khi giá trong nước điều chỉnh chậm hơn, trước hết phản ánh sự khác biệt về cung - cầu và cơ chế truyền dẫn giá giữa hai thị trường”, ông Nhân nói.
Theo ông Nhân, về dài hạn, đây là tín hiệu tích cực. Khi người dân có thêm lựa chọn giữa vàng, tiền gửi và các tài sản tài chính khác, thị trường vàng có thể bớt đầu cơ, giá trong nước vận động sát hơn với quốc tế và giảm tình trạng dòng tiền tập trung quá mức vào vàng.
Nhận định về triển vọng giá vàng, ông Nhân cho rằng thời gian tới vàng vẫn có xu hướng duy trì ở mặt bằng cao và còn dư địa tăng, song mức độ biến động sẽ rất lớn.
“Tôi cho rằng ngưỡng 4.600 USD/ounce hiện nay là vùng tâm lý rất quan trọng. Nếu giá duy trì được trên vùng này, động lượng tăng có thể tiếp tục và thị trường có thể hướng tới những vùng giá cao hơn. Một số tổ chức quốc tế vẫn duy trì triển vọng tăng dài hạn của vàng, trong đó J.P. Morgan đưa ra kịch bản vàng có thể hướng tới 6.000 USD/ounce”, ông Nhân cho hay.
Với thị trường trong nước, vị chuyên gia dự báo giá vàng vẫn có thể tiếp tục đi lên nhưng khả năng tăng chậm hơn giá thế giới.
Ông Nhân đặc biệt lưu ý không nên biến vàng thành kênh đầu cơ ngắn hạn. Khi giá đã ở vùng cao, chỉ cần USD phục hồi, lợi suất tăng hoặc Fed phát tín hiệu thắt chặt hơn, vàng hoàn toàn có thể điều chỉnh mạnh.
Về dài hạn, theo chuyên gia, mục tiêu không phải kìm giá vàng tăng hay giảm mà là mở rộng nguồn cung hợp pháp, tăng cạnh tranh và minh bạch hóa thị trường. Khi giá vàng trong nước phản ánh sát hơn cung - cầu và giá quốc tế, tình trạng đầu cơ, găm giữ vàng có thể giảm, qua đó tạo điều kiện để dòng vốn được phân bổ vào sản xuất, kinh doanh và các kênh đầu tư dài hạn.

articles.title: New York Times AI summaries are now live for some readers
articles.text:
The New York Times has started showing readers text written by a machine. A new search page answers queries with excerpts, links to Times stories and AI-generated summaries of Times reporting. Max Tani, Semafor’s media editor, reported the test on Sunday.
The paper rolled it out quietly to a small subset of visitors over recent weeks. It is the news arm’s first test of AI-generated text that no Times journalist or editor has passed.
The Times hopes the tool will fix a search feature Semafor describes as troubled. Some of the paper’s own journalists are alarmed by it.
What the Times says
“We are always testing new ways for our users to discover and engage with Times journalism,” spokesperson Graham James told Semafor.
“This experimental feature is an example of how we are using the latest technology to create a better search experience.”
What the tool is not
The summaries draw on Times journalism and nothing else. This is not a chatbot answering questions about the world, and it does not reach across the open web.
That narrows the failure modes without removing them. A summary of accurate reporting can still misstate what the reporting said.
Wirecutter got one first
The Times has been running AI features in its non-news sections for months. Wirecutter, its review site, recently started testing a search tool called Wirecutter Finder. It points readers to AI-generated summaries and tips drawn from the site’s own recommendations.
Those experiments have stayed outside the newsroom. The search summaries do not.
The paper has also given its journalists internal AI tools for their own work for some time. Those sit behind the reporting rather than in front of the reader.
The union found out at the bargaining table
Times management told its union it would test AI summaries in search during a contract bargaining session in July. The media newsletter Breaker, written by Lachlan Cartwright, reported that on 7 August, describing a heated session. Semafor cited the report this week.
The announcement caused frustration inside the company’s editorial union. The union says the Times is breaking its own editorial standards on AI use.
What the union wants
The Times Guild has put a set of AI rules on the table. One would create an employee payment pool, splitting 22.5% of the paper’s AI licensing deals for training data among unionised staff.
Another would require human oversight of any AI use. That clause would make the new search tool impractical to run.
‘Meaningless’
Jim Luttrell, the Guild unit chair and a senior staff editor, said the paper’s current AI policies are “meaningless”.
“Management can change and even violate the company’s policy in any way they want, as they are doing with the summarization tool,” he told Semafor.
“Every time AI summaries have been deployed, they have made embarrassing mistakes. That’s why we need strong guardrails on AI in the contract, to protect readers’ trust in our journalism.”
Why the paper is doing it
Search and summarisation tools are now standard across websites, apps, inboxes and rival news organisations. Semafor described the Times as playing catch-up.
Several Times employees told Semafor the change is necessary. Search has long lagged the paper’s other publishing products, they said, which Semafor calls otherwise best in class.
The talks are still running. Management and the Guild returned to the bargaining table this month with the AI clauses unresolved.
The accuracy problem
A few sentences summarising the paper’s own reporting is not an ambitious use of the technology. It is a harder call for the Times than for most publishers, Semafor argued, because the institution runs on layers of fact-checking and editing.
The paper still makes mistakes and appends corrections. What it has built is a system for catching them first, and a reputation that rests on that system.
There is also an incentive for bad actors. Semafor raised the prospect of someone spending all day trying to trip the summariser into saying something stupid. The paper’s political opponents are looking for ways to discredit its journalism.
It has gone wrong elsewhere
The Washington Post trialled an AI-generated podcast feature that produced errors and fictional quotes, Semafor reported in December.
Other publishers have leant harder on the technology and paid for it. BuzzFeed cut another third of its staff after betting on AI.
AI text is spreading either way
Pew found strong signs of AI authorship in around 10% of webpages it sampled in July.
That is the environment the Times has spent the AI era positioning itself against.
Deepfakes, bots and hallucinations have made the basic question of what is real harder to answer. News organisations have responded by selling themselves as the places where a human checked the work.
Taking the human out, even in a few sentences on a search page, cuts against that pitch. Semafor made the point plainly, and it is the argument the union is making inside the building.
The money underneath it
Publishers are being pulled towards AI from several directions at once. OpenAI is funding 13 Axios local newsletters under a three-year deal.
Google, meanwhile, wants publishers to install a button that makes readers pick them inside its own products.
The Times has its own reasons to want readers staying longer. It fell short on digital subscriber growth in the second quarter.
What has not been said
The Times has not said which model generates the summaries, how many readers are seeing them, or how long the test runs.
It has not said whether the summaries carry a label, or what happens when one of them gets something wrong.
And it has not said whether the feature goes beyond the test group, or what would stop it if the union got its clause.
